title: Thirty-five years, 32 moments
lede: From a slowing soft drink market to a rumor about 2027. Choose a thread to narrow the list.

events.title: A $47 billion market slows
events.text: PepsiCo later tells shareholders that by 1991 US soft drinks were a $47 billion retail business, “but growth had begun to slow down.”

events.title: Work begins on a clear cola
events.text: Pepsi says development took about 15 months and nearly 3,000 variations. The start date is derived from the April 1992 announcement.

events.title: Test markets announced
events.text: Crystal Pepsi is to go on sale in Providence, Dallas and throughout Colorado, in clear 16-ounce and 2-liter bottles and silver cans.

events.title: Deep discounts in the test
events.text: A Providence chain sells two-liter bottles for 39 cents with coupons, while a Dallas store manager calls the drink “just a novelty.”

events.title: A diet version joins
events.text: PepsiCo dates the introduction of both Crystal Pepsi and Diet Crystal Pepsi to late 1992.

events.title: National introduction
events.text: After test-marketing since April, the regular and diet versions are introduced nationally.

events.title: Coca-Cola unveils Tab Clear
events.text: At the Hayden Planetarium in New York. Doug Ivester says “Clear Coke is an oxymoron.” It is a sugar-free diet cola with caffeine.

events.title: Pepsi projects more than 2%
events.text: Pepsi says Crystal Pepsi will take more than 2% of the $47 billion market in its first national year, about $1 billion at retail.

events.title: Best new product of the year
events.text: Richard Saunders International puts Crystal Pepsi at the top of its “Pure Gold” list of new grocery products. PepsiCo’s annual report says Time also named it one of the year’s best.

events.title: Tab Clear on sale
events.text: In 10 US markets, and in London from mid-January, the first overseas rollout.

events.title: Advertising begins
events.text: The campaign starts on the eve of President Clinton’s inauguration.

events.title: Super Bowl XXVII
events.text: The national advertising, estimated at $40 million, runs in the game with the theme “You’ve never seen a taste like this.”

events.title: Wrapped buses
events.text: Six buses covered end to end in Crystal Pepsi advertising go into service in San Francisco and Oakland, at nearly $3,000 a month each.

events.title: “One share point means $474 million”
events.text: Jesse Meyers of Beverage Digest tells The New York Times the brand earned a full share point. The same article reports the launch of Pepsi Max abroad.

events.title: Clear is called a fad
events.text: The Associated Press counts about four dozen clear products among 16,790 new products in 1992. Miller plans a clear beer.

events.title: The one good quarter
events.text: PepsiCo later says the Crystal Pepsi products “particularly aided first quarter results.”

events.title: Caught in the syringe hoax
events.text: During a wave of false tampering claims against Pepsi, a California woman admits inventing a report about a can of Diet Crystal Pepsi.

events.title: “Crystal Gravy”
events.text: Saturday Night Live runs a mock commercial for clear gravy.

events.title: An ice rink
events.text: The Crystal Pepsi Ice Skating Rink opens at Universal CityWalk for the holidays, a year after one in San Francisco.

events.title: Coke writes the obituary
events.text: Roberto Goizueta is quoted as saying both Tab Clear and Crystal Pepsi “are about to die.” Quoted from a 2018 article citing Adweek.

events.title: “Softening trends”
events.text: PepsiCo’s 1993 annual report says the product is being refined and will return in 1994 in a nondiet version only.

events.title: “Deemed a dud”
events.text: The New York Times reports the clear colas are “undergoing an overhaul.” A test commercial for the new version runs in four markets.

events.title: Crystal, without the Pepsi
events.text: The citrus cola reformulation reaches stores nationwide, labeled “From the makers of Pepsi,” with no summer advertising.

events.title: “Significant declines”
events.text: PepsiCo’s annual report and 10-K record significant declines in the Crystal Pepsi brands. Its end date is not recorded.

events.title: “The best idea I ever had, and the worst executed”
events.text: David Novak, by then chief executive of Yum Brands, gives his verdict to Fast Company.

events.title: A 20-year-old bottle
events.text: Kevin Strahle, known as L.A. Beast, posts a video of himself drinking one.

events.title: PepsiCo answers the campaign
events.text: Strahle posts a message from Pepsi: “we think you’ll all be happy with what’s in store.” A spokeswoman confirms it is genuine.

events.title: Sweepstakes
events.text: 13,000 six-packs are offered through the Pepsi Pass app.

events.title: Back in stores
events.text: On sale in Canada from July 11 and in the United States from August 8, in 20-ounce bottles at $1.79.

events.title: “One last limited time”
events.text: A second retail run follows a three-city Throwback Tour. PepsiCo calls it “Crystal Pepsi’s last return.”

events.title: Thirtieth anniversary
events.text: 300 contest winners receive six bottles each. The drink is not sold.

events.title: A rumor about 2027
events.text: Social media accounts report a return in May 2027, but PepsiCo has not confirmed it.
